svg.title: Stabilizer lifting and a unitary correction
svg.desc: For the countable Schreier-induced actions of Theorem 2A.1, cocycle conjugacy to the simple centre lifting is equivalent to a genuine unitary representation lifting the stabilizer automorphisms. The S4 example has anticommuting implementers and fails this condition. The S3 example has a cyclic stabilizer implemented by P with P squared equal to one, and admits an explicit correction despite failing original descent.

g.text: A nonfree action can admit a unitary correction
X = Y × K/H; Γ = ℤ × K. Use the Schreier-induced fibre action of Theorem 2A.1.
The exact criterion for this family
φ : H → Int(N) lifts to V : H → U(N), with Ad(Vh) = φ(h) and VhVk = Vhk.
⇔ There are an α-cocycle u and normal θ with θ αᵘ θ⁻¹ = β.
A lift gives θ = id and u(n,k)(y,d) = Vκ(k,k⁻¹d)*. No amenability is needed for this equivalence.
If vhvh′ = c(h,h′)vhh′, the scalar equation is λhλh′ c(h,h′) = λhh′.
S₄ : the obstruction persists
H = ⟨a,b⟩ ≅ C₂ × C₂; E has probability 1/6.
φ(a) = Ad P; φ(b) = Ad Q; PQ = −QP.
Scalar phases preserve this commutator.
Commuting generators cannot lift to P and Q.
No cocycle and normal conjugacy give β.
Theorem 2.3; Theorem 2A.1; Corollary 2A.2.
S₃ : a correction exists
H = ⟨h⟩ ≅ C₂; E has probability 1/3.
Ve = 1 and Vh = P form a representation.
The original action fails descent on E.
But u = W* gives αᵘ = β, with θ = id.
Exercise 6.6; the centre action is faithful and ergodic.

Source context: Takesaki III, Chapter XIII, §4, Exercise 1, printed page 79. No general stabilizer-field criterion is asserted.
